 Jock Landale (hip) is questionable to return to Saturday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Landale played for one minute before leaving Saturday’s game with a left hip injury. If he can’t return, Asa Newell will likely play rotation minutes off the bench. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jock Landale (hip) will not return to Saturday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Landale played just over one minute before exiting Saturday’s game in the first quarter with a left hip injury. Asa Newell has entered the rotation off the bench and could retain that role if Landale misses time beyond Saturday. 
 Jock Landale 
 ATL 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jock Landale (nose) is available for Friday’s game against the Hornets. 
 Landale, who played 19 minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s win over the Magic, is dealing with a broken nose. He’ll take on his usual responsibilities as Onyeka Okongwu’s backup, which limits the veteran center’s fantasy value. 
 Jock Landale 
 ATL 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jock Landale recorded 17 points (7-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, three steals, two blocks and one three-pointer in Monday’s exhibition against the Thunder. 
 With Onyeka Okongwu off on Monday night, Landale started against the Thunder. The veteran center had a productive night at the office, reminding everyone of his streaming value. Landale isn’t a player who should be selected in 12-team drafts, but fantasy managers should be mindful of him if Okongwu sits due to injury. 
 Asa Newell 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Asa Newell led the Hawks with 15 points (5-of-11 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in a 93-66 win over the Spurs on Thursday. 
 Newell has been productive in his second summer league on both ends of the floor. He needs to continue to improve as a shooter to have a chance to crack the Hawks’ rotation this season, though. He shot 1-of-3 from deep in this game and is just 3-of-12 this summer. The volume is encouraging, but he still has more growing to do as a rebounder, defender and floor spacer, even if he has developed considerably since entering the NBA already. 
 Asa Newell 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Asa Newell produced 13 points (5-of-8 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s win over the Thunder. 
 After a solid showing in Saturday’s summer opener, Newell shot the ball better on Monday. His improved efficiency in that area is encouraging for the Hawks, who rarely called Newell’s number during his rookie season. That said, rebounding and defense will likely need to be his calling cards if he’s to crack Quin Snyder’s rotation once the regular season begins. 
 Asa Newell 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Asa Newell finished with 15 points (5-of-15 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Jazz on Saturday. 
 Newell didn’t have his best shooting performance from deep, but he got up plenty of shots from deep and looked confident as a shooter. That’s going to help him get on the floor, but the other factor is how well he can defend down low and rebound. He still has a ways to go on that end, even if he does look noticeably stronger than he did as a rookie. 
 Jock Landale 
 ATL 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jock Landale and the Hawks have agreed to a one-year contract worth $14 million. 
 Between the Grizzlies and Hawks, Landale appeared in 67 games in 2025-26. Serving mainly as Onyeka Okongwu’s backup until a high ankle sprain ended his season in early April, the 6-foot-11 center averaged 9.1 points and 4.1 rebounds in 19.4 minutes for the Hawks. Landale’s return fortifies Atlanta’s center rotation, which the team added to in the draft by selecting Zuby Ejiofor with the 23rd overall pick. 
 Jock Landale 
 ATL 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jock Landale (ankle) will be re-evaluated in two weeks. 
 Landale will miss the first round of the playoffs. The 30-year-old center sustained a high ankle sprain against the Magic on April 1 and has progressed in his rehabilitation, but isn’t ready to return yet. Mo Gueye and Tony Bradley will be the backup center options for the Hawks in their series against the Knicks. 
 Asa Newell 
 ATL 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Asa Newell recorded a double-double on Sunday with 17 points (7-of-13 FGs), 10 rebounds, two assists, one block and one three-pointer against the Heat. 
 Newell got the starting nod for Atlanta with the typical starters getting a rest night in Game 82. The rookie took advantage of the opportunity and recorded the first double-double of his young career. The Hawks’ first-round pick hasn’t played a significant role for them, but he still has plenty of upside and could take on more minutes in his second season. He likely won’t see the floor much during the playoffs, but he is still worth stashing in dynasty formats. 
 Jock Landale 
 ATL 
 Center 
 #31 
 Jock Landale (ankle) will be re-evaluated in two weeks. 
 Landale has been diagnosed with a high right ankle sprain sustained during the fourth quarter of Wednesday’s win over the Magic. With the two-week timeline being for a re-evaluation, the veteran backup is not guaranteed to be available when the playoffs begin. Landale’s injury leaves Mouhamed Gueye to serve as the backup center in the short term. As for the playoffs, starter Onyeka Okongwu will likely be asked to take on a heavier workload if Landale is not back by then.

 Kenrich Williams finished Saturday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers.
 After totaling 10 points in his first two starts of the season, Williams scored 11 on Saturday. He was most valuable against the Rockets in three-pointers and rebounds, but this performance doesn’t make “Kenny Hustle” a must-add heading into Oklahoma City’s four-game Week 3. Also, with the Thunder playing two games against Cleveland to start the week, it’s fair to wonder whether head coach Mark Daigneault would consider a bigger lineup to match up with Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. If so, Williams or Jared McCain (10/4/2/1) could be headed to the bench.

 Isaiah Hartenstein amassed 10 points (3-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and three steals in Saturday’s loss to the Rockets.
 With Chet Holmgren (knee) out for at least 8-10 weeks, the Thunder will rely even more on Hartenstein, Jaylin Williams (3/4/1/1) and Aday Mara (seven points, nine rebounds, three assists and four blocks) in the post. Of the three, Hartenstein is the safest option for fantasy managers, which is why he’s rostered in over 80 percent of Yahoo leagues.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tallied 26 points (10-of-20 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Rockets.
 Since the October 25 game against the Clippers in which Oklahoma City lost Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, Gilgeous-Alexander has shot 49.1 percent from the field and 5-of-17 from beyond the arc. Of course, the Thunder have also lost Chet Holmgren since last Sunday, which allows opposing teams to devote even more attention to slowing down SGA. Fantasy managers will hope his efficiency doesn’t take too big a hit in the weeks to come. Oklahoma City plays four games next week, starting with two against the Cavaliers on Monday (away) and Wednesday (home).

 Alperen Şengün finished Saturday’s win over the Thunder with 16 points (6-of-17 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), nine rebounds, nine assists and one block.
 Şengün returned to the Rockets lineup after sitting out Friday’s loss to the Mavericks with a sore back. He played 33 minutes and finished one rebound and one assist shy of a triple-double. Turnovers can still be an issue for Şengün at times, but he’s gotten off to a good start this season. Clint Capela, who started on Friday, recorded four rebounds and two assists in 10 minutes.

 Marcus Smart accumulated 24 points (7-of-10 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Thunder.
 Smart started Saturday night, as the Rockets did not have Fred VanVleet (knee) due to injury management. The veteran guard shot 7-of-10 from beyond the arc against the Thunder and recorded his first regular-season 20-point game since March 14 against the Nuggets, when he played for the Lakers. While Smart will be a fixture in the Rockets’ rotation, his fantasy outlook hinges on VanVleet’s availability.

 Jabari Smith Jr. produced 30 points (10-of-18 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), nine rebounds, five assists, one block and six three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Thunder.
 Smith matched his season high with 30 points, recording the seventh 30-point game of his NBA career on Saturday. Against the Thunder, he shot 6-of-12 from three, helping the Rockets compensate for Fred VanVleet’s absence and a relatively quiet night from Kevin Durant (14/3/4/1/3). Smith has gotten off to an excellent start, leaving some to decide whether to “sell high” or bet he continues to play this well. The Rockets play three games next week, starting with the Celtics on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Domantas Sabonis recorded 11 points (3-of-5 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 14 rebounds, eight assists and one steal in Saturday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
 Fantasy managers rostering Sabonis received solid returns in rebounds and assists. However, the Kings center took just five shots on Saturday, matching his season low. Sabonis is averaging 9.2 attempts per game, his fewest since 2018-19. Zach LaVine (11 points, one assist) attempted nine shots on Saturday. With rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. having the ultimate “green light,” it will be interesting to see how vets like Sabonis and LaVine adjust. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 De’Andre Hunter amassed 19 points (8-of-18 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
 While Hunter’s streak of 20-point games didn’t reach three on Saturday, he did hit double digits in shot attempts for the third straight game. His fantasy value has been limited for most of his career, especially in category leagues, because he hasn’t produced much in assists, steals, or blocks. However, Hunter’s recent scoring run and Keegan Murray’s continued absence make him someone to consider adding in deep leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darius Acuff 
 SAC 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Player Stats

 Darius Acuff Jr. finished Saturday’s loss to the Grizzlies with 38 points (12-of-25 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and nine three-pointers.
 After six games, it’s clear the Kings won’t impose any offensive limitations on Acuff. While efficiency can be an issue at times, that was not the case on Saturday. Acuff established new highs in points and three-pointers while shooting a respectable 48 percent from the field. He was especially good in the first half, scoring 21 points on 7-of-13 shooting and committing one turnover. The Kings play four games next week, starting with the Mavericks on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Gregory Jackson 
 MEM 
 Small Forward 
 #45 
 Player Stats

 GG Jackson recorded 21 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, two assists and five three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Kings.
 Jackson entered Saturday having made four of 13 three-point attempts over five games. Going 5-of-5 as he did against the Kings will give the three-point percentage a welcome boost, all the way up to 50 percent. Scoring in double figures for the third time in six games, Jackson also posted a season-high 21 points against the Kings. He still isn’t worth fully committing to in most fantasy leagues. However, GG may be worth considering in certain matchups, especially on nights when the Grizzlies are down a key scorer (Ty Jerome didn’t play on Saturday).
